<div id="S1.SS1.SSS3.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.SSS3.p12.1" class="ltx_p">We note that the initial Facebook100 dataset included gender information as a feature. We chose not to include gender as one of the features, as it has been shown that language models exhibit gender bias <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>, <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>. An example of the prompt using real-world social network data is given at <a href="#alg1" title="In A.1.2 Prompts ‣ A.1 Experimental Procedure ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS1.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.1.4 </span>Robustness Checks and Prompt Sensitivity</h4>

<div id="S1.SS1.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We tried the following LLM models:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-3.5 (<span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-3.5-turbo</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-4o Mini (<span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Llama 3 (<span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">llama-3-70b-instruct</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Claude 3.5 Sonnet (<span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620</span>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For each of the models except Claude 3.5 we used three temperatures: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5. For the Claude 3.5 model we used temperatures 0.5 and 1.0 (since the model does not allow temperatures above 1.0). Finally, we experimented with different contexts (e.g., friendship, collaboration, community) to test prompt sensitivity.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Details for Small-World Experiments</h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The algorithm for the altered Watts-Strogatz model is described as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S1.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Similarly to Watts-Strogatz, we first create a ring network with <math id="S1.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> nodes. After that, for each node <math id="S1.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[n]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[n]</annotation></semantics></math>, we create <math id="S1.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> edges where <math id="S1.I2.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k/2</annotation></semantics></math> edges connect to its rightmost neighbors and <math id="S1.I2.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k/2</annotation></semantics></math> edges connect to its leftmost neighbors.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To create <math id="S1.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, for each node <math id="S1.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[n]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[n]</annotation></semantics></math>, we take its <math id="S1.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k/2</annotation></semantics></math> rightmost neighbors and rewire them with probability <math id="S1.I2.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. For each of the <math id="S1.I2.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k/2</annotation></semantics></math> rightmost neighbors that are to be rewired, we make one query to the LLM, which indicates how the edge will be rewired. The choice is made by providing the LLM with all the network nodes and each node’s neighbors (i.e., the network structure).</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The model closely resembles the Watts-Strogatz model, with the primary distinction being the method of edge rewiring. Instead of randomly selecting edges for rewiring, as in the Watts-Strogatz model, we determine the rewiring of an edge by inquiring about the LLM and providing it with the current network structure.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Real-World Network Experiments</h3>

<section id="S1.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.1 </span>The Discrete Choice Model in Real-World Network Experiments</h4>

<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each node <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> that we consider at time <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we randomly remove one of its current friends from the real-world network. After we remove a neighbor for each of <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{1},\dots,i_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{1},\dots,i_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, we end up with the network <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, which we use as a seed network for the LLM agents.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Subsequently, during the link formation process, we present each node <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> with a set of candidate nodes (denoted by <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>), comprising one of the previously removed friends and other nodes that are not their friends. We then instruct the LLM to form a link with one of the candidates, providing the attributes of the candidates and the social network structure to aid its decision-making. These choices are made sequentially.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We use the <span id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">utility</span> of the model for each node for each sequential decision of network formation:</p>
<table id="S1.EGx7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.Ex6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle U_{ij,t}=\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}\log d_{j,t}+\theta_{\mathrm{H}}\log w_{ij}+\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}\log c_{ij,t}+\epsilon_{ij,t}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>PA</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>TC</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle U_{ij,t}=\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}\log d_{j,t}+\theta_{\mathrm{H}}\log w_{ij}+\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}\log c_{ij,t}+\epsilon_{ij,t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In this equation, <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>PA</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures the strength of preferential attachment based on the degree <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{j,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{j,t}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> at step <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\mathrm{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\mathrm{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures the strength of homophily based on the similarity <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e. number of common attributes) between <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>TC</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}</annotation></semantics></math> measures the strength of triadic closure, based on the number of common neighbors <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{ij,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{ij,t}</annotation></semantics></math> between <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> at step <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. The error term <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{ij,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{ij,t}</annotation></semantics></math> is distributed as i.i.d. standard Gumbel.<span id="footnote11" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">11</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              The standard Gumbel distribution has CDF <math id="footnote11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{e^{-x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{e^{-x}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></span>
All variables are first normalized based on their range, and then the log transformation is taken.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The multinomial logit model (MNL) indicates that the probability that <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> links to <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> at step <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S1.EGx8" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle p_{ij,t}=\Pr\left[\mathrm{argmax}_{r\in A_{t}}U_{ir,t}=j\right]=\frac{d_{j,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{ij}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{ij,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}}{\sum_{r\in A_{t}}d_{r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{ir}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{ir,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">p</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">Pr</mi><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">argmax</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">A</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">U</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">w</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><mrow><msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">A</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">w</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.900em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle p_{ij,t}=\Pr\left[\mathrm{argmax}_{r\in A_{t}}U_{ir,t}=j\right]=\frac{d_{j,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{ij}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{ij,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}}{\sum_{r\in A_{t}}d_{r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{ir}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{ir,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Given a sequence of nodes <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{1},\dots,i_{T}\in V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{1},\dots,i_{T}\in V</annotation></semantics></math> and choices (denoted by subscripted <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>) <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{1}\in A_{1},\dots,j_{T}\in A_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{1}\in A_{1},\dots,j_{T}\in A_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, the parameters can be found by maximizing the log-likelihood function. To get the standard errors of the coefficients and the corresponding <math id="S1.SS3.SSS1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-values, we follow the process outlined in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.2 </span>Estimating the Parameters of the Discrete Choice Model</h4>

<div id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To estimate the parameters of the discrete choice model, we optimize the following log-likelihood function:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S1.EGx9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle(\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}})=\argmax_{(\theta_{\mathrm{PA}},\theta_{\mathrm{TC}},\theta_{\mathrm{H}})\in\mathbf{R}^{3}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigg(\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}\log d_{j_{t},t}+\theta_{\mathrm{H}}\log w_{i_{t}j_{t}}+\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}\log c_{i_{t}j_{t},t}-\log\big(\sum_{r\in A_{t}}d_{r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{i_{t}r}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{i_{t}r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}\big)\bigg)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">max</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">𝐑</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">3</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">log</mi><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">log</mi><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">w</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">log</mi><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">log</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" movablelimits="false" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">A</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">d</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">PA</mi></msub></msubsup><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">w</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi></msub></msubsup><msubsup><mi mathsize="0.900em">c</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">r</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi></mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">θ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">TC</mi></msub></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle(\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}})=\argmax_{(\theta_{\mathrm{PA}},\theta_{\mathrm{TC}},\theta_{\mathrm{H}})\in\mathbf{R}^{3}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigg(\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}\log d_{j_{t},t}+\theta_{\mathrm{H}}\log w_{i_{t}j_{t}}+\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}\log c_{i_{t}j_{t},t}-\log\big(\sum_{r\in A_{t}}d_{r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{PA}}}w_{i_{t}r}^{\theta_{\mathrm{H}}}c_{i_{t}r,t}^{\theta_{\mathrm{TC}}}\big)\bigg),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{1},\dots,i_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{1},\dots,i_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> are the chooser nodes (i.e., the LLM agents who want to form a link), and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{1},\dots,j_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>j</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{1},\dots,j_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> are the nodes which are chosen from the alternative sets <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{1},\dots,A_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{1},\dots,A_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. The likelihood function is convex, and we optimize it with the L-BFGS-B method <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>. The standard errors of the coefficients are approximated as <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{-H^{-1}/N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{-H^{-1}/N}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is the Hessian matrix of the log-likelihood at <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>PA</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>TC</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}},\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of data points (cf. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.3 </span>Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions</h4>

<div id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At each decision step <math id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, a query node <math id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> selects a link from a set of candidate nodes <math id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Given the limited context window of LLMs, we consider two alternative strategies for constructing the candidate set <math id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uniform Sampling.</span> We uniformly sample <math id="S1.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> non-neighbor nodes from the graph. This approach serves as a neutral baseline, ensuring that the alternatives presented to the model are selected without structural or feature-based bias. Uniform sampling reflects a scenario where the agent has no <em id="S1.I3.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">a priori</em> ranking or filtering of candidates and evaluates all choices purely based on the features provided in the prompt.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Recommendation-Based Sampling.</span> We use a supervised link prediction model based on logistic regression to compute the likelihood of a link between each candidate pair <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{i,j\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{i,j\}</annotation></semantics></math> following the work of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>. The probability of <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{i,j\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{i,j\}</annotation></semantics></math> being an edge equals <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\left(\psi^{T}z_{ij}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ψ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\left(\psi^{T}z_{ij}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is the sigmoid function, <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math> is a vector of trainable parameters, and <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij,t}=\left(w_{ij},c_{ij,t},d_{i,t}\cdot d_{j,t},\sum_{k\in N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)}\frac{1}{\log|d_{k,t}|},\frac{|N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)|}{|N_{t}(i)\cup N_{t}(j)|}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij,t}=\left(w_{ij},c_{ij,t},d_{i,t}\cdot d_{j,t},\sum_{k\in N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)}\frac{1}{\log|d_{k,t}|},\frac{|N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)|}{|N_{t}(i)\cup N_{t}(j)|}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is the feature vector for the pair <math id="S1.I3.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{i,j\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{i,j\}</annotation></semantics></math> with the following entries:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.I3.i2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I3.i2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Similarity</span> between node attributes <math id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Number of common neighbors</span> <math id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{ij,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{ij,t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Preferential attachment score</span> <math id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i,t}\cdot d_{j,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i,t}\cdot d_{j,t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adamic-Adar index</span> <math id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{k\in N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)}\frac{1}{\log|d_{k,t}|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{k\in N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)}\frac{1}{\log|d_{k,t}|}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<div id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Jaccard Similaririty</span> between node neighborhoods <math id="S1.I3.i2.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{|N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)|}{|N_{t}(i)\cup N_{t}(j)|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{|N_{t}(i)\cap N_{t}(j)|}{|N_{t}(i)\cup N_{t}(j)|}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.I3.i2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To avoid structural bias due to the LLM agents, the logistic regression model is trained at <math id="S1.I3.i2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., prior to any link formation by the LLM agents, as:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.I3.i2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S1.EGx10" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.Ex7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\hat{\psi}=\argmax_{\psi\in\mathbf{R}^{5}}\left\{\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_{+}}\log\sigma\left(\psi^{T}z_{ij,1}\right)+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_{-}}\log\left(1-\sigma(\psi^{T}z_{ij,1})\right)\right\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ψ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>max</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ψ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>ij</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mo>−</mo></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ψ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>ij</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\hat{\psi}=\argmax_{\psi\in\mathbf{R}^{5}}\left\{\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_{+}}\log\sigma\left(\psi^{T}z_{ij,1}\right)+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_{-}}\log\left(1-\sigma(\psi^{T}z_{ij,1})\right)\right\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S1.I3.i2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I3.i2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{+}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{-}</annotation></semantics></math> are equally sized sets of positive and negative edges sampled from <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. For each <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the set <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is presented to the LLM agent, is constructed as the top-<math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> highest-scoring nodes concerning node <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, where the scores are computed as <math id="S1.I3.i2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i_{t},j}=\sigma(\hat{\psi}^{T}z_{i_{t}j,t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ψ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i_{t},j}=\sigma(\hat{\psi}^{T}z_{i_{t}j,t})</annotation></semantics></math>. To train the logistic regression model, we use the <span id="S1.I3.i2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">statsmodels</span> Python package. Information about the parameters of the link prediction algorithms can be found in <a href="#S2.SS2.SSS1" title="B.2.1 Recommendation System Parameters ‣ B.2 Robustness of Results to Sampling Strategies ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.4 </span>Measuring Alignment Between Models</h4>

<div id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The plots of <a href="#Sx2.F5" title="In Hyperparameters. ‣ Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ Decisions on Real-World Networks with Heterogeneous Agents ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> are constructed by measuring similarity between models. Specifically, for two LLM models <math id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, we fit two discrete choice models <math id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> respectively according to <a href="#S1.E2" title="In A.3.1 The Discrete Choice Model in Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equations</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and <a href="#S1.E3" title="Equation 3 ‣ A.3.2 Estimating the Parameters of the Discrete Choice Model ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and measure the following:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spearman correlation Between Effects.</span> We measure <math id="S1.I4.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}},\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Spearman</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}},\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, which measures the difference in how the different LLM models rank preferential attachment, homophily, and triadic closure.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TV Distance Between Fitted Models.</span> We measure the total variation distance between the probabilities that each LLM model assigns to nodes parametrized by the MNL model. Specifically, the TV distance is calculated by sampling a time index <math id="S1.I4.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly in <math id="S1.I4.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,T\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,T\}</annotation></semantics></math> and a pair of a node <math id="S1.I4.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and an alternative set <math id="S1.I4.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S1.I4.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.I4.i2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S1.EGx11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

</div>
<div id="S1.I4.i2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I4.i2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In our implementation, we report the Monte-Carlo estimate of <a href="#S1.E4" title="In 2nd item ‣ A.3.4 Measuring Alignment Between Models ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Human Baseline</h3>

<section id="S1.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.1 </span>Survey</h4>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct the survey by presenting three alternatives (<math id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=3</annotation></semantics></math>) to each participant in two different contexts (social network, company network). For each participant <math id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, and each context <math id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega\in\{\text{Social Network},\\
\text{Company}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>Social Network</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>Company</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega\in\{\text{Social Network},\\
\text{Company}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we generate a dynamic survey with alternative set <math id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math>. For each alternative <math id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in A_{i,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in A_{i,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math> we generate:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S1.I5" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Number of friends (degree) <math id="S1.I5.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{j,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{j,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math> .</span> Uniformly sampled integer between 0 and 1000.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Number of common friends (common neighbors) <math id="S1.I5.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{ij,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{ij,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> Uniformly sampled integer between 0 and the number of friends (degree).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Similarity <math id="S1.I5.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{ij,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{ij,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> Uniformly sampled integer between 0 and 10 for the social network context, indicating the number of common interests. Uniformly sampled binary variable determining the role of the person (0 for co-worker, 1 for manager).</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For the social network context, we ask the participant (focus profile) to pretend to be a college student. For the company network context, we ask the participant to pretend to be an employee (non-manager). The participants are asked how they ranked – from 1 to 3 (1 = worst, 3 = best) – the three attributes when forming their decision and optionally give the reasoning behind their decisions.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">IRB Approval.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Cornell University (Protocol #IRB0150009), and all participants provided informed consent prior to participation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.2 </span>Sample Size Construction on Prolific</h4>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We distribute the survey on the Prolific platform on participants located in the United States, who are at least 18 years old and speak English as their primary language. We obtain <math id="S1.SS4.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=100</annotation></semantics></math> responses for the social network context, and <math id="S1.SS4.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=103" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>103</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=103</annotation></semantics></math> responses for the company context. We use the standard sampling settings for prolific. Participants are allowed to submit the survey only once.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.3 </span>Measuring Alignment between models and Humans</h4>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each participant <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, context <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega\in\{\text{Social Network},\text{Company}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>Social Network</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>Company</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega\in\{\text{Social Network},\text{Company}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and alternative set <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math> we construct <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{ij,\omega}=\left(d_{j,\omega},c_{ij,\omega},w_{ij,\omega}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{ij,\omega}=\left(d_{j,\omega},c_{ij,\omega},w_{ij,\omega}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> for each <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in A_{i,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in A_{i,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math>. We let <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}\in A_{i,\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}\in A_{i,\omega}</annotation></semantics></math> to be the decision of model/human <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> abd <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> to be the vector of Borda counts for the choice <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>. For instance, if a human participant ranked homophily over triadic closure over preferential attachment, their Borda score vector is <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i,\omega}^{\mathrm{Human}}=(1,2,3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi>Human</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i,\omega}^{\mathrm{Human}}=(1,2,3)</annotation></semantics></math> assuming that the first dimension corresponds to preferential attachment (number of friends), the second dimension corresponds to triadic closure (number of common friends), and the third dimension corresponds to homophily (similarity).</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Between-Model Agreement.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each model <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> we fit a discrete choice model <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> similarly to <a href="#S1.SS3.SSS1" title="A.3.1 The Discrete Choice Model in Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3.1</span></a>. We also calculate the average Borda Score vector as <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>ω</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To measure between-model agreement we compare the pairs of models according to the following criteria:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S1.I6" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I6.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Principle-Level.</span> For each pair of models we measure <math id="S1.I6.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}},\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Spearman</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}},\hat{\theta}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I6.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{TV}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{M}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{TV}(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{M}^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> similarly to <a href="#S1.E4" title="In 2nd item ‣ A.3.4 Measuring Alignment Between Models ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I6.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Choice-Level.</span> For each pair of models we measure <math id="S1.I6.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}},\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Spearman</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>ω</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>ω</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Spearman}\left(\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}},\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> and the distance <math id="S1.I6.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\|\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}-\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>ω</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>ω</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msubsup></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\|\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}-\bar{h}_{\omega}^{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}\right\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Within-Model Agreement.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To measure the within-model agreement for model <math id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> we measure the average Spearman correlation of the Borda count vectors between pairs of participants, i.e.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S1.EGx12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.Ex8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{1}{\binom{n}{2}}\sum_{i,j:i&lt;j}\mathrm{Spearman}\left(h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}},h_{j,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mi>Spearman</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{1}{\binom{n}{2}}\sum_{i,j:i&lt;j}\mathrm{Spearman}\left(h_{i,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}},h_{j,\omega}^{\mathcal{M}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Survey Prompt.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the prompt described in <a href="#alg3" title="In Survey Prompt. ‣ A.4.3 Measuring Alignment between models and Humans ‣ A.4 Human Baseline ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.3</span></a> for the survey data.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg3" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
