<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.4 </span>Robustness Checks and Prompt Sensitivity</h4>

<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We tried the following LLM models:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I7" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I7.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-3.5 (<span id="S1.I7.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-3.5-turbo</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I7.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I7.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GPT-4o Mini (<span id="S1.I7.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I7.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I7.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I7.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Llama 3 (<span id="S1.I7.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">llama-3-70b-instruct</span>)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I7.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I7.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I7.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Claude 3.5 Sonnet (<span id="S1.I7.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620</span>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Additionally, to measure alignment with humans we use data collected from humans through the Prolific platform</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Temperatures.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each of the models except Claude 3.5 we used three temperatures: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5. For the Claude 3.5 model we used temperatures 0.5 and 1.0 (since the model does not allow temperatures above 1.0). In the main paper we report results with temperature equal to 0.5. The results are robust to temperature change (see <a href="#S2.T4" title="In B.3.1 Regression Coefficients ‣ B.3 Robustness of Results to Temperature ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.4</span></a> for results with other temperatures).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Context Window Length.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform robustness checks regarding the size of the context window. We use the large context window model gpt-4.1-mini and context windows <math id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A\in\{50,100\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>50,100</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\in\{50,100\}</annotation></semantics></math> (see <a href="#S2.SS4" title="B.4 Robustness of Results to Large Context Windows ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sampling Strategies.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform robustness checks with two policies for generating the alternative sets <math id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>: (i) uniform sampling and (ii) sampling based on a recommendation system based on logistic regression.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt Sensitivity.</h5>

<div id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS4.SSS4.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform prompt sensitivity experiments based on the different contexts and the type of experiment: (i) decisions in real-world networks with real-world data, where we use <a href="#alg2" title="In A.1.2 Prompts ‣ A.1 Experimental Procedure ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.2</span></a>, (ii) survey data, where we use <a href="#alg3" title="In Survey Prompt. ‣ A.4.3 Measuring Alignment between models and Humans ‣ A.4 Human Baseline ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.3</span></a>. Our findings are robust to different prompts.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Data and Code Availability</h3>

<div id="S1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Data and code are openly available on GitHub at the following link:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><a href="https://github.com/papachristoumarios/llm-network-formation" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/papachristoumarios/llm-network-formation</a></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The real-world social network data have been taken from the sources of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">B </span>Real-World Datasets</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Statistics of Real-World Datasets</h3>

<figure id="S2.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2402.10659v7/Facebook100_Caltech36_stats.png" id="S2.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/112;" width="234" height="112" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2402.10659v7/Facebook100_Swarthmore42_stats.png" id="S2.F1.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/112;" width="234" height="112" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2402.10659v7/Facebook100_Uchicago30_stats.png" id="S2.F1.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/112;" width="234" height="112" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><img src="2402.10659v7/Andorra_stats.png" id="S2.F1.g4" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:234/110;" width="234" height="110" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>

</section>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S2.T1" title="In B.2.1 Recommendation System Parameters ‣ B.2 Robustness of Results to Sampling Strategies ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.1</span></a> shows the effects and the AUC score for the recommender system based on logistic regression (cf. <a href="#S1.SS3.SSS3" title="A.3.3 Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ A.3 Real-World Network Experiments ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.2 </span>Change in Graph Statistics due to Different Sampling Strategies</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across all datasets and models, the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics indicate that adding a small fraction of new edges (<math id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 5\%</annotation></semantics></math>) produces only minor shifts in the degree distribution, spectrum, and sizes of connected components, with most p-values far above the 0.05 threshold. Significant changes arise primarily in the local clustering coefficient—particularly under the Uniform strategy—suggesting localized structural effects without major disruption to global network properties. In contrast, the Recommendation System strategy yields even fewer significant differences, with most metrics remaining statistically indistinguishable from the original graphs. These results indicate that, at this perturbation scale, LLM-driven edge additions preserve the overall network structure, with strategy choice influencing the extent of local structural change.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T2" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S2.T2.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S2.T2.2.1" class="ltx_tr">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:50%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table SI.2: </span><span id="S2.T2.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Change in Graph Statistics for the experiments of <a href="#Sx2.T1" title="In Hyperparameters. ‣ Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ Decisions on Real-World Networks with Heterogeneous Agents ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</span> We report the KS statistic and the P-values for the following quantities (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> for more information on the statistics): (i) degree distribution, (ii) distribution of the sizes of strongly connected components, (iii) adjacency matrix spectrum, (iv) local clustering coefficient. The last column reports the percentage of new edges added. Adding <math id="S2.T2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo mathsize="2.000em">%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of edges based on LLM decisions leaves global graph properties largely unchanged, with only occasional local clustering increases—more frequent under the Uniform strategy than the Recommendation System.</figcaption>
</figure>

</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.3 </span>Average Marginal Effects</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S2.T3" title="In B.2.3 Average Marginal Effects ‣ B.2 Robustness of Results to Sampling Strategies ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.3</span></a> we report the average marginal effects (AMEs) per feature for the experiments of <a href="#Sx2.T1" title="In Hyperparameters. ‣ Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ Decisions on Real-World Networks with Heterogeneous Agents ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Our analysis reveals that LLM-driven edge formation is consistently shaped by preferential attachment and homophily, with homophily often exhibiting the largest marginal effects – frequently exceeding 1.0 and reaching above 2.5 under the Recommendation System strategy. Preferential attachment is positive across all datasets and models, indicating a systematic tendency to link to high-degree nodes. Triadic closure effects are more variable, sometimes reinforcing local clustering and sometimes favoring cross-community connections, particularly under the Recommendation System. Compared to Uniform edge additions, the Recommendation System generally amplifies both preferential attachment and homophily, suggesting that recommendation-driven link formation intensifies these social-network-like biases.</p>
</div>

<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Robustness of Results to Temperature</h3>

<section id="S2.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.3.1 </span>Regression Coefficients</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S2.T4" title="In B.3.1 Regression Coefficients ‣ B.3 Robustness of Results to Temperature ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.4</span></a>, we report the regression coefficient for the regression in the real-world network data for all temperatures and GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview). The first column corresponds to the temperature, the next three columns correspond to the fitted coefficients from the regression model of Section 1.C (also shown in Figure 5) accompanied by the standard errors (in parentheses) and the <math id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-values indicated by stars (the null hypothesis corresponds to the parameters being set to 0). Next, LL corresponds to the log-likelihood of the fitted model, and AIC corresponds to the Akaike Information Criterion. Finally, we report the percent change in the accuracy compared to random guessing, the percent change in the average path length (as a measure of the small-world phenomenon), and the clustering coefficient (as a measure of the small-world phenomenon and the triadic closure), as well as the <math id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-statistic for the change in modularity (<math id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>) between the ground truth network dataset (before the edge deletions) and the network after the network formation process.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We observe that <math id="S2.SS3.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>TC</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>PA</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{H}}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{TC}}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PA}}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> accross all settings. LLM agents do better than random guessing, reinforce the small-world phenomenon, and weaken the triadic closure, though the changes are very small, 0-1% change for the average path length and up to 10% change for the clustering coefficient. Finally, the community structure is strengthened after new links are formed.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:50%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table SI.4: </span>Multinomial logit coefficients for three networks from the Facebook100 dataset and GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview). The standard errors of the estimates are shown in parentheses. The null hypothesis corresponds to the respective parameter being equal to 0. We report the percent change in accuracy, average path length, and average clustering coefficient compared to the initial network (before the deletion of edges). For the change in modularity, we run the Louvain algorithm ten times and perform a t-test with the resulting modularities. For the UChicago30 dataset, we report the t-statistic value in the subgraph induced by the 2,000 sampled nodes, since the newly added edges would have a very small effect on the change in the community structure if we were to measure it in the whole network. We also report the modularity change (t-statistic) of the whole graph inside brackets.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.3.2 </span>Change in Graph Statistics due to Different Temperatures</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Further, to measure the changes in the network statistics, we use the metrics presented in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> to quantify the changes. Specifically, we measure the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and the corresponding <math id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-value for the degree distribution, the distribution of the sizes of the connected components, the distribution of the singular values of the adjacency matrix, and the distribution of the local clustering coefficient, (CC) for the real-world Facebook100 networks and the gpt-4-1106-preview model (the results are similar for the other networks and models we examined). Except the changes on the distribution of the sizes of the connected components for UChicago30, we find that most KS statistics are negligible and the corresponding <math id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-values are large (e.g. <math id="S2.SS3.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\gg 0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P\gg 0.5</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that most network statistics are not affected. <a href="#S2.T5" title="In B.3.2 Change in Graph Statistics due to Different Temperatures ‣ B.3 Robustness of Results to Temperature ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.5</span></a> summarizes the results:</p>
</div>

<section id="S2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Robustness of Results to Large Context Windows</h3>

<div id="S2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform experiments with the large-context model gpt-4.1-mini. We set the temperature to 0.5. <a href="#S2.T6" title="In B.4 Robustness of Results to Large Context Windows ‣ B Real-World Datasets ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.6</span></a> shows the effect sizes. We observe that for social networks (Caltech36, Swarthmore42, UChicago30) homophily still remains the dominant force for large context windows and that in most cases <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}_{H}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{TC}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{PA}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}_{H}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{TC}&gt;\hat{\theta}_{PA}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, agreeing with the results of <a href="#Sx2.T1" title="In Hyperparameters. ‣ Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ Decisions on Real-World Networks with Heterogeneous Agents ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Additionally, for the MobileD network we observe heterophily (<math id="S2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}_{H}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}_{H}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>). On the other hand, we observe that for the Andorra dataset, for larger contexts, the triadic closure has a positive effect (<math id="S2.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\theta}_{TC}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\theta}_{TC}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>) compared to negative weight in <a href="#Sx2.T1" title="In Hyperparameters. ‣ Candidate Set Construction for Network Decisions ‣ Decisions on Real-World Networks with Heterogeneous Agents ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (<math id="S2.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T6" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S2.T6.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S2.T6.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T6.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="S2.T6.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Dataset</span></td>

<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">C </span>Network Evolution and Omitted Simulations</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here we depict the evolution of the networks generated by the LLM agents, as well as omitted simulations.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Principle 1: Preferential Attachment</h3>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Network Evolution</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We plot the evolution of the LLM-based preferential attachment networks at three timesteps, together with the degree distribution alongside the degree distribution of a BA graph with the same number of nodes. We observe that for the temperature being 0.5 we have a core-periphery-like formation which diverges from the BA model, whereas for the temperature being 1.5 the network has the same degree distribution as the BA model.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_1_200_0_0.5_neighbors.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/102;" width="381" height="102" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_1_200_0_1.0_neighbors.png" id="S3.F2.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/101;" width="381" height="101" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_1_200_0_1.5_neighbors.png" id="S3.F2.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/101;" width="381" height="101" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.2: </span>Dynamic evolution of networks created based on Principle 1.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Simulations with Degree Information</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#S3.F3" title="In Simulations with Degree Information ‣ C.1 Principle 1: Preferential Attachment ‣ C Network Evolution and Omitted Simulations ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.3</span></a> we provide the results with degree-information only. We observe that the agents form connections around high-degree nodes only (see <a href="#S3.F3" title="In Simulations with Degree Information ‣ C.1 Principle 1: Preferential Attachment ‣ C Network Evolution and Omitted Simulations ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.3</span></a>). The same result (star-like networks) holds for the other LLM models and temperatures.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_1_final_graphs.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/108;" width="429" height="108" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.3: </span><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Results for Principle 1 (preferential attachment):</span> We display simulated networks comprising 200 nodes across different temperatures. For the degree-based simulations, node degree data <math id="S3.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{d_{j,t}:j\in V_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{d_{j,t}:j\in V_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> was provided (<math id="S3.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the vertex set of the network <math id="S3.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> at round <math id="S3.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>). With degree information only, the networks form more unrealistic star-like structures, diverging from scale-free configurations and more closely mirroring a core-periphery network structure.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Principle 2: Triadic Closure</h3>

<section id="S3.SS2.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Network Evolution</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We plot the evolution of the LLM-generated networks based on the triadic closure principle, together with the transitivity measure and the algebraic connectivity (which corresponds to the second-smallest eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian). We observe that the algebraic connectivity gradually increases as new edges between the clusters are created. Specifically, the algebraic connectivity reaches a higher value for higher temperatures, indicating the more frequent creation of new intra-cluster edges. Moreover, we observe that the transitivity initially increases and then decreases until it reaches its final value.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_2_50_0_0.5_neighbors.png" id="S3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/96;" width="381" height="96" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_2_50_0_1.0_neighbors.png" id="S3.F4.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/96;" width="381" height="96" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_2_50_0_1.5_neighbors.png" id="S3.F4.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/96;" width="381" height="96" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.4: </span>Dynamic evolution of networks created based on Principle 2.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Simulations with the Number of Common Neighbors</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Instead of giving the neighborhood information, the simulations presented in <a href="#S3.F5" title="In Simulations with the Number of Common Neighbors ‣ C.2 Principle 2: Triadic Closure ‣ C Network Evolution and Omitted Simulations ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.5</span></a> use the number of common neighbors. We observe behavior similar to <a href="#Sx2.F2" title="In Principle 2: Triadic Closure ‣ Micro-Level Properties ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2402.10659v7/principle_2_final.png" id="S3.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/86;" width="429" height="86" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.5: </span><span id="S3.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Results for Principle 2 (triadic closure).</span> The figure shows the same networks as in <a href="#Sx2.F2" title="In Principle 2: Triadic Closure ‣ Micro-Level Properties ‣ Results ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> with the only change that instead of the intersection of neighborhoods between the query node and each alternative, we provide the number of common neighbors (i.e., the size of the intersection) between the query node and each alternative. Similarly, we observe that the probability of forming an edge within the same community and the marginal transitivity, which indicate triadic closure, is significantly larger than randomly creating links (<math id="S3.F5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>, t-test). The error bars correspond to 95% confidence intervals.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Principle 5: Small-World Phenomenon</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S3.F6" title="In C.3 Principle 5: Small-World Phenomenon ‣ C Network Evolution and Omitted Simulations ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.6</span></a> shows LLM-generated small-world networks for <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}</annotation></semantics></math> and compares them with the Watts-Strogatz networks with the same parameters.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F6.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(a)</span> </span><math id="S3.F6.sf1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.800em">β</mi><mo mathsize="0.800em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.800em">0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0.25</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F6.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(b)</span> </span><math id="S3.F6.sf2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.800em">β</mi><mo mathsize="0.800em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.800em">0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0.5</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F6.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(c)</span> </span><math id="S3.F6.sf3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.800em">β</mi><mo mathsize="0.800em">=</mo><mn mathsize="0.800em">0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0.75</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.6: </span><span id="S3.F6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Simulation results for Principle 5 (small world).</span> Network instances for the networks created according to Principle 5 using the altered Watts-Strogatz Model for node count <math id="S3.F6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=50</annotation></semantics></math>, average degree <math id="S3.F6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=5</annotation></semantics></math>, rewriting probability <math id="S3.F6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}</annotation></semantics></math>, together with plots of the <span id="S3.F6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">average clustering coefficient</span> <math id="S3.F6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> and the <span id="S3.F6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">average shortest path length</span> <math id="S3.F6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>. The comparison is made with respect to a Watts-Strogatz graph with <math id="S3.F6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=50,k=5,\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.75</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=50,k=5,\beta\in\{0.25,0.5,0.75\}</annotation></semantics></math>. The error bars correspond to 95% confidence intervals. The results are compared against the Watts-Strogatz model with the same parameters <math id="S3.F6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.F6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> as a null model. The t-test comparing <math id="S3.F6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.F6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> for the LLM-generated networks and Watts-Strogatz networks yields <math id="S3.F6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&gt;0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&gt;0.05</annotation></semantics></math> (Bonferroni correction for two tests).</figcaption>
</figure>

</section>
</section>

<div id="lstnumberx184" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx184.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx184.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">-</span><span id="lstnumberx184.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">You</span><span id="lstnumberx184.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">can</span><span id="lstnumberx184.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">make</span><span id="lstnumberx184.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">at</span><span id="lstnumberx184.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">most</span><span id="lstnumberx184.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">1</span><span id="lstnumberx184.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx184.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">selection</span><span id="lstnumberx184.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">.</span>
</div>
</div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We experiment with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">60</a>]</cite>. To induce CoT reasoning we ask the LLM agents to output the reason and then their choice (i.e. by reversing the order of <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">reason</span> and <span id="S4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">name</span> in <a href="#alg2" title="In A.1.2 Prompts ‣ A.1 Experimental Procedure ‣ A Methods and Materials ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.2</span></a>). The resulting prompt can be found at <a href="#alg4" title="In D Chain-of-Thought Experiments ‣ Network Formation and Dynamics among Multi-LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">SI.4</span></a>. In the following figures, we show the results from the same experiments as the ones we of the main text with the different that CoT is used.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F7.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2402.10659v7/probabilitytopk_cot.png" id="S4.F7.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:286/92;" width="286" height="92" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S4.F7.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Probability of connecting to top-<math id="S4.F7.sf1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> nodes for different models, temperatures, and environments</span></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F7.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S4.F7.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Power law fits (<math id="S4.F7.sf2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo mathsize="1.250em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>) and standard errors for different models, temperatures, and environments</span></figcaption>

</figure>

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F8.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2402.10659v7/triadic_closure_cot.png" id="S4.F8.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:322/241;" width="322" height="241" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F8.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S4.F8.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Marginal transitivity (<math id="S4.F8.sf2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>) and probability of an edge within a community (<math id="S4.F8.sf2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo mathsize="1.250em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p}</annotation></semantics></math>) for different models, temperatures, and environments</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.8: </span><span id="S4.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Results for Principle 2 with CoT reasoning (triadic closure).</span> <span id="S4.F8.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top:</span> Probability of connecting to top-<math id="S4.F8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> nodes (in terms of common neighbors) for varying model (temperature is fixed to 1.0 and environment to baseline), temperature (model fixed to GPT-4 Mini and environment to baseline) and environment (model fixed to GPT-4 Mini and environment temperature to 0.5) for networks generated according to Principle 2 (<math id="S4.F8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=50</annotation></semantics></math>, 10 simulations for each model, environment and temperature). <span id="S4.F8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bottom:</span> Marginal transitivity (<math id="S4.F8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>) and probability of an edge within a community (<math id="S4.F8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p}</annotation></semantics></math>) for networks generated according to Principle 2 in different models, temperatures, and environments.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<figure id="S4.F9.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><img src="2402.10659v7/assortativities_cot.png" id="S4.F9.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/235;" width="429" height="235" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F9.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S4.F9.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Assortativity and Louvain Modularity with different LLM models and environments</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.9: </span><span id="S4.F9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Results for Principle 3 (Homophily) and Principle 4 (Community structure due to homophily) with CoT reasoning.</span>
<span id="S4.F9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top:</span> Assortativities and Louvain modularity according to Principle 3 (<math id="S4.F9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=50</annotation></semantics></math>, 5 simulations for each row) in different environments (school, work, community) using different models. The statistical significance is <math id="S4.F9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.0003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.0003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.0003</annotation></semantics></math> for all t-tests (comparing with 0, Bonferroni correction for three tests).</figcaption>
</figure>

</figure>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure SI.10: </span><span id="S4.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fitted results for Principle 5 with CoT reasoning (small world).</span> Regression plot for the relation <math id="S4.F10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\sim\log(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\sim\log(n)</annotation></semantics></math> for different LLM models for <math id="S4.F10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0.25</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.F10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=5</annotation></semantics></math>. The legend shows the effect size (<math id="S4.F10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>) and the <math id="S4.F10.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-value. (*: <math id="S4.F10.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.0025" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.0025</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.0025</annotation></semantics></math>; **: <math id="S4.F10.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.005</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.005</annotation></semantics></math>, and ***: <math id="S4.F10.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P&lt;0.0005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.0005</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P&lt;0.0005</annotation></semantics></math>, Bonferroni correction for two tests).</figcaption>
